facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burned out since October. He feels exhausted and is running on fumes.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October.

facts.heading: Work overload and burnout
facts.content: Daniel works as a project manager at a logistics company. He is thinking about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I work as a project manager at a logistics company, and I've been completely burned out since October.

facts.heading: Long working day routine
facts.content: Daniel stays at his desk until ten at night. He thinks about work outside of work hours.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night. Even when I'm not working I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible. He sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours.

facts.heading: Waking up at three AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Thoughts during wakefulness
facts.content: When Daniel wakes up, his mind focuses on work and logistics. He calculates how little sleep he will get, which worsens the situation.
facts.evidence: My head just starts. Shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something. Then I look at the clock and do the maths on how little sleep I'm going to get, which makes it worse.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights. He lies there until about five before getting up.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current condition
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated. He is seventy-three years old.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, and he's slower, and he gets frustrated. He's seventy-three and he's always been the strong one.

facts.heading: Driving father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments. These appointments are every few weeks and take an hour each way.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. The neurology appointments are every few weeks, and it's an hour each way.

facts.heading: Sole caregiver role
facts.content: Daniel is the only one caring for his father because his younger sister lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: All the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Feeling guilty about tiredness
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for being tired when his father is ill. He does not say anything to anyone.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill. So I don't say anything to anyone.

facts.heading: Sister's involvement
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah calls their father every Sunday. Hannah is not neglecting him.
facts.evidence: She calls him every Sunday, and she's not the one who's neglecting him.

facts.heading: Responding to sister's questions
facts.content: When Hannah asks how Daniel is, he says fine. He does not share the truth about his exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine.

facts.heading: Desire to reveal feelings
facts.content: Daniel does not want to tell Hannah the truth about his state. He feels he cannot face it.
facts.evidence: That I'm not fine. That some days I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before I go in, because I can't face it.

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests that were all normal. The GP suggested stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests, and they were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked therapy
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire booked a session for him. Claire said she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is patient and makes Daniel tea without pushing him to talk. Claire is also wearing on.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk. But I can see it's wearing on her too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking about trips
facts.content: Claire stopped asking if Daniel wanted to go away for the weekend. Daniel always says no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend, because I always say no.

facts.heading: Emails cause anxiety
facts.content: Daniel receives two hundred emails if he is away. He worries Dad might need something.
facts.evidence: If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them. And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: Stopped running recently
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. His legs felt like lead, and he never went back.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs felt like lead, and then I just never went back.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself after stopping running. He felt running was the one time nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Cannot picture time
facts.content: Daniel cannot picture where the time would come from to get back what he lost.
facts.evidence: I just can't picture where the time would come from.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss Peterson sends emails at eleven at night. He expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: Peterson. He's all right as a person, but he sends emails at eleven at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answers emails constantly
facts.content: Daniel answers every email, even when he is in bed. Claire hates this behavior.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid Peterson will think he isn't committed. There is a restructuring in the spring and he fears being let go.
facts.evidence: That he'd think I wasn't committed. There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Ambivalent about job loss
facts.content: Daniel thinks he might feel relieved if he is let go, but he would also feel horrible about it due to his mortgage.
facts.evidence: I think part of me would be relieved, and then I'd feel horrible about being relieved. I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Mood is flat and irritable
facts.content: Daniel's moods apart from tiredness are flat and irritable. He snapped at a colleague and sat in the toilets.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable. I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.

facts.heading: Panic attack symptoms
facts.content: When Daniel snapped at a colleague, his heart was going and his hands were shaking. He briefly thought it was a heart attack.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking. I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Frightening event on train
facts.content: Daniel has had frightening experiences on the train to Manchester. He had to get off and stand on the platform.
facts.evidence: Once on the train to Manchester. I just had to get off and stand on the platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that he is losing it. He is afraid of not coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Evening wine consumption
facts.content: Daniel has started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off. He drinks two to three glasses.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine effect on sleep
facts.content: Daniel finds the wine is not helping with sleep. He wakes up at three anyway.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Wine as listing problems
facts.content: Daniel feels the wine makes him list everything wrong with himself.
facts.evidence: It feels like I'm just listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Relief from speaking out
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief when speaking about his feelings.
facts.evidence: Strange. A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Desire to sleep
facts.content: Daniel thinks that if he could sleep, he could probably cope with the rest.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family influence on coping
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything. His father is similar.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once. Dad's the same. You just get on with it.

facts.heading: Belief about being weak
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being there.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Self-talk about weakness
facts.content: Daniel stated he would tell his grandfather he is not weak but tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. I'm just very tired.

facts.heading: Belief about self-talk
facts.content: Daniel is unsure if he believes he can say this to himself.
facts.evidence: Maybe. I don't know if I believe it yet.

facts.heading: Proposed coping strategy
facts.content: Daniel was asked about trying something small between now and next week.
facts.evidence: Would you be willing to try something small?

facts.heading: Proposed evening routine
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try switching off his phone for twenty minutes at half past nine.
facts.evidence: Yes. Half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.heading: Planning to track sleep
facts.content: Daniel offered to write down how the night goes if he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I can do that. I'll write down when I wake up, if I wake up.

facts.heading: Current feeling after session
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after the session.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.

facts.heading: Agreed to meet next week
facts.content: Daniel agreed to meet again next week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yes. I'll be here.
